data.name: Nirmala
data.gender_notes: Nirmala is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit nir, 'without', + mala, 'stain' — 'spotless, pure'. Its root is Sanskrit nir + mala. A classical Sanskrit term for purity. Nirmala is a Sanskrit name meaning “Pure; spotless; clean”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Nirmala expresses “Pure; spotless; clean”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit nir, 'without', + mala, 'stain' — 'spotless, pure'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nirmala total 32, reducing to 5. Number 5 is associated with freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Nirmala is used in Sanskrit naming tradition with the meaning “Pure; spotless; clean”.

vedic_reference.note: Nirmala is the name of the goddess Lakshmi in her pure form.

historical_references.reference: A classical Sanskrit term for purity.
